unresolvedReferences.description: 悼恭太子 died before Xianzong learned of the boy. No year is numbered. English Youji is not in the Chinese.
The sacrifice to Confucius is not a year of his own life.
Yu Qian receives a posthumous title. The text does not date his life or death.
The eldest imperial son is born unnamed. The next year names the imperial son Houzhao. They are taken as one son because the text distinguishes no other.
Taizu is named only as the emperor with whom meritorious men were enshrined. No year of his life is given.
English Jing Jian Ze splits 見潚 and uses Jing, the same English word as 涇王 above. The Chinese title here is 荊王.
Chang Yuchun, Li Wenzhong, Deng Yu, and Tang He appear only as ancestors whose descendants were enrolled.
The grand empress dowager is ill. Her surname is not given in this chunk, and she is not said to have died.
Yang Shi enfeoffment is posthumous. Confucius is named only as the temple in which Yang Shi was associated.
潮河川 is the Chao River valley. The English Chaohu names a different lake.
楊翥 is Yang Zhu. The English Yang Chong is a different reading.
The First Teacher temple at Qufu burned. That is not a year of Confucius life.
李鐩 is Li Sui. The English Li Yong uses a different reading.

The grand empress dowager died. Her surname is not written in this chunk.
